sections.h2: How can I sell a Cheektowaga house without a long listing?
sections.html:
Cheektowaga owners can hire an agent, sell without one, or deal directly with a company like ours. The direct route appeals to anyone who wants to skip repairs, showings and a buyer's loan approval, and it gives you control of the closing date.

Cheektowaga is a town in Erie County and the second-largest suburb of Buffalo after Amherst. It contains the village of Sloan and half of the village of Depew, and the rules that apply to your house can change depending on whether it lies in the town outside the villages. Check your tax bill first.

sections.h2: What do the Census figures show for Cheektowaga?
sections.html:
An estimated 88,160 people lived in town in mid-2025, below the 89,877 of the 2020 census and above the 88,226 of 2010.

A median value of $185,000 compares with $164,200 in Buffalo and $332,700 for the country. About 19.7% of residents are 65 or older, so estate sales and downsizing move a share of the houses.

sections.h2: How did Cheektowaga grow from farmland to a suburb?
sections.html:
Chictawauga, the Seneca name for the area, translates to land of the crabapples. Cheektowaga was formed from the Town of Amherst on March 22, 1839, and it reached its present size after West Seneca separated in 1851. Population grew from 25,006 in 1940 to 45,354 in 1950, then 84,056 in 1960 and a peak of 113,844 in 1970.

According to Wikipedia, a rural farming area was developed into suburban housing during the 1950s subdivision boom, helped along by new highways and by employers such as the Westinghouse plant on Genesee Street. About 39.9% of residents claim Polish ancestry, many of them families who moved out from Buffalo's East Side. The Walden Galleria opened in 1989 and is the largest mall in the Buffalo Niagara region.

That postwar growth means many Cheektowaga houses date from the 1950s and 1960s, so a buyer's inspector will likely focus on mechanical systems and the age of the shingles.

sections.h2: Which neighborhoods and roads define Cheektowaga?
sections.html:
Cheektowaga borders Buffalo on the west, Amherst on the north, Lancaster on the east and West Seneca on the south. Wikipedia lists a string of neighborhoods, and several have their own school districts.

  • Bellevue, between Union Road and the Depew line
  • Cleveland Hill, on the north town line, with its own school district
  • Maryvale, west of the airport, which is also a school district
  • Pine Hill, on the Buffalo border near Villa Maria College
  • Doyle, South Line and U-Crest in the south and southwest
  • Sloan, a village and the seat of the Cheektowaga-Sloan school district

Eight separate public school districts operate inside the town, so a buyer's first question is often which one covers the house. Buffalo Niagara International Airport, Erie County's main airport, lies within the town, and Villa Maria College and Empire State University have campuses here.

The New York State Thruway, I-90, crosses the town from north to south. Union Road (NY 277), Harlem Road (NY 240), Transit Road (NY 78) and Broadway (NY 130) carry local traffic, and the Kensington Expressway (NY 33) and I-190 lead toward Buffalo.

Cheektowaga lies in the lake-effect snow band, and Wikipedia lists the Blizzard of '77, the Blizzard of '85, the October Surprise storm, Snowvember and the 2022 Christmas blizzard among its historic events. Tornadoes have also touched down near Union Road, an F1 that grew to F2 on July 30, 1987 and another F1 on June 30, 2006, and both damaged homes and businesses without causing deaths.

When a roof has been patched more than once or a basement takes on water in spring thaw, the repair estimate can exceed what a seller wants to spend. An as-is cash sale lets you pass the repair to the buyer rather than paying for it first.

sections.h2: Must a Cheektowaga landlord register with the town?
sections.html:
Yes, if you own property in the town outside the villages of Sloan and Depew and you do not live there. Chapter 194 of the town code, the Landlord Rental and Property Owner Registration Ordinance, requires registration every two years whether the building is occupied or vacant.

  • The registration fee is $20.
  • A registration statement is due within 30 days of buying the property.
  • Failing to register violates section 194-6 and carries a fine.

For a rental or a vacant inherited house, bring the registration up to date before closing. The town's Building Department covers building, plumbing, fire safety and neighborhood preservation, and the registration page is published by the Town Clerk and Receiver of Taxes.

sections.h2: What happens at the Erie County Clerk and the Town Assessor?
sections.html:
Deeds for Cheektowaga houses are recorded at the Erie County Clerk. Transfer tax runs $4.50 for each $500 of price, made up of $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for the county, and the seller owes it when the TP-584 is filed. A seller aged 62 or older who has owned and lived in a one- or two-family house for at least a year can drop the rate to $2.00 per $500 with an affidavit. On a $185,000 sale, the standard tax is $1,665 and the reduced tax is $740.

One percent Mansion Tax applies once the price on a residential conveyance reaches $1 million. Residential sales also require a Notice of Sale or Transfer of Ownership form. The clerk's office cannot help fill out legal forms, so a lawyer or title agent normally drafts the documents.

The Cheektowaga Assessment Office, phone 716-686-3440, can confirm your assessed value, and the town website posts the tentative and final assessment rolls. Ask the office whether your parcel has an exemption on file before you sell.

sections.h2: What steps should a Cheektowaga seller take first?
sections.html:
Four items keep a quick sale on track.

  • Confirm from the deed and tax bill whether the house is in the town outside the villages or inside Sloan or Depew.
  • Register the property with the town if you do not live in it, and pay the $20 fee.
  • Get a payoff figure from your lender, and ask the Assessment Office whether the parcel carries exemptions.
  • Gather the deed, the TP-584 and the RP-5217 so the Erie County Clerk can record the transfer at closing.

With median household income at $69,239 and owners in 71.5% of homes, most sellers here are individual homeowners. A direct buyer can build the closing around a mortgage payoff, a probate timeline or your move date.

faqs.q: Is Cheektowaga a city or a town?
faqs.a: It is a town in Erie County. It contains the village of Sloan and half of the village of Depew, and it sits next to Buffalo on the city's east side.

faqs.q: What does Cheektowaga charge to register a non-owner-occupied house?
faqs.a: The fee is $20. Registration repeats every two years, and the first statement is due within 30 days after you buy.

faqs.q: Is there a senior discount on Cheektowaga transfer tax?
faqs.a: Yes. Erie County allows owners aged 62 or older to reduce the rate from $4.50 to $2.00 per $500 if they owned and lived in a one- or two-family home for at least a year before the sale. The affidavit is free at the County Clerk's office.
The town Assessment Office, reachable at 716-686-3440. Its website also carries the tentative and final assessment rolls.

faqs.q: Which school district serves a given Cheektowaga house?
faqs.a: Eight public districts operate within the town, among them Cheektowaga-Sloan, Maryvale and Cleveland Hill. The answer depends on the parcel, so verify with the district before telling a buyer.
